title: docs(concepts): add How ObjectStack compares and When to use ObjectStack
body:
Fixes #22240
Clause-②: no

Two hand-written positioning pages under Core Concepts, English only, plus the wiring the card's Part C names. Docs-only: no `packages/**`, no `apps/docs/**`, no `content/blog/**`, no `README.md`, no `content/docs/references/**`, no `content/docs/releases/**`, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no binaries.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| :--- | :--- |
| `content/docs/concepts/compare.mdx` | new, How ObjectStack compares (Part A) |
| `content/docs/concepts/when-to-use.mdx` | new, When to use ObjectStack, and when not to (Part B) |
| `content/docs/concepts/meta.json` | `compare`, `when-to-use` inserted after `ontology` |
| `content/docs/concepts/ontology.mdx` | one pointer sentence closing "What it is not", one closing the page; nothing else |
| `content/docs/concepts/index.mdx` | one sentence naming both pages, in the paragraph that introduces the ontology |
| `scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json` | regenerated by `node scripts/docs-audit/check-audit-scope.mjs --write` (+2 added, -0 removed); not hand-edited |

## Measurements (head e0c7be11)

| Page | Body words (`wc -w` after frontmatter) | `description` chars | `title` chars |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| compare.mdx | 1074 | 155 | 64 |
| when-to-use.mdx | 870 | 152 | 40 |

Both descriptions are real summaries inside the 110 to 160 range.

## Facts about ObjectStack, and where they come from

- Federation: early and read-only by default, writes behind a double opt-in, per `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx` (section 5) and the existing wording on `concepts/ontology`.
- Agent access: the MCP server is on by default, objects are tools, actions are tools only when the author exposes them (`ai.exposed`), permissions decide what an agent may call, per `ai/connect-mcp` and `ai/actions-as-tools`.
- No number appears on either page. See the CRM-size note under Acceptance notes.

## Vendor facts dropped or narrowed (the card's rule: drop rather than guess)

1. Operational ontologies: "open-source reference implementations of the same pattern exist" is dropped. I could not trace it to a named public source.
2. Metadata platforms: "most of which added MCP servers in 2025 and 2026" is narrowed to "Several of them now offer MCP servers". Public docs confirm MCP servers for Salesforce (hosted MCP servers), NocoBase (MCP plugin), Twenty (marked alpha), Payload (MCP plugin) and Frappe (an experimental package). I found no first-party Odoo server, and the dates are not confirmed for every product.
3. Metadata platforms: "their metadata is configuration held in a database and authored in a UI" is narrowed to "In most of these platforms ...; where it is code, as with the Payload Config or Odoo's modules, it is framework code". Payload is configured in TypeScript and Odoo models are Python modules, so the card's sentence was not true of every named example.
4. AWS Context is named as a category example, with no availability status: public sources disagree on preview versus GA.
5. Microsoft Fabric IQ: "in preview" is kept behind "As of late 2026". The Learn overview marks the Ontology item as preview.

No star counts, market claims, analyst quotes, "the only" or "the first" appear. Products are named only as examples after the category is described. The table carries one line saying each cell reads a category as a whole.

## Gates (all on head e0c7be11, exit code captured before any pipe)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build` under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`: `VERDICT command-exit 0` (held the lock 84s). Both pages render: `/en/docs/concepts/compare` and `/en/docs/concepts/when-to-use` are emitted.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derives 50 commands. All 50 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation over a record carrying exit codes reports: 50 derived, 50 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, a derived zero.
- These include `check:doc-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:docs-redirects`, `check:docs-single-h1`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`, `check:published-readme-links`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:role-word`, `check-doc-frontmatter`, `check-doc-route-spelling --advisory`, `check-section-landing-index`, and the lint package's `check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:doc-security-posture`.
- I also ran four that were named in the dispatch but are not in the derivation: `check:docs-locale-catch-all`, `check:page-declaration-shape`, and `check-docs-nav-label` (self-test and real run). All exit 0.
- An earlier round on a prior head had two problems. First, three gates exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET, which measures nothing; they went green after their packages were built (`@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/client-react`). Second, `check:role-word` exited 1 because the five-questions list used the reserved word for access. It now uses the permission-set vocabulary of ADR-0090.
- NOT MEASURED locally: the lychee link check (CI only), the Test Core and type-check lanes (no TypeScript touched), and the `Build Docs` CI job itself. The local docs build runs the same package script.

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured CRM size: card premise vs. the tree.** The card allows one number, "the example CRM's size as the ontology page states it". `concepts/ontology` states no size. The figure lives on `concepts/metadata-driven` and `getting-started/how-ai-development-works` (1,792 lines across 31 files). That figure has drifted: the page's own count command, run on 3ae59661, prints 1,929 lines across 31 files. So `when-to-use` states no number and links to the measurement section instead. The drift is reported to the dispatching seat. It is outside this PR's file surface.
- **Try it link.** The card's "Try it (quick-start)" points at a page that calls itself "the map, not a starting point" and sends builders to Build with Claude Code. "Try it" therefore links Build with Claude Code, and the quick-start page (Anatomy of an ObjectStack App) is linked beside it.
- **Opening paragraph.** Two of the five sections the card asks for (metadata platforms, AI code generation) do not use the word "ontology". The opening says "three that use the word and two that answer the same question without it" rather than "four kinds of ontology and ObjectStack is a fifth".
- Changeset: none. Nothing publishes. `packages/**` is untouched, and no published package's `files[]` ships `content/` or `scripts/docs-audit/`.
